sections.h2: Who sends and collects a Warren County tax bill
sections.html:
The job is split among three Bowling Green offices that take calls on weekdays. The PVA sets the value, the sheriff mails the bill and collects, and the clerk inherits whatever is still open after April 15.

  • PVA: 429 E. 10th Avenue, Bowling Green, KY 42101, phone (270) 843-3268, open 8:00 to 4:30.
  • Sheriff: (270) 842-1633, with a tax inquiry page for looking up and paying a bill. The business office keeps the same 8:00 to 4:30 hours.
  • County Clerk: P.O. Box 478, Bowling Green, KY 42102, phone (270) 842-9416. Property tax and valuation questions go to the PVA.

The sheriff collects under KRS 134.140 and 160.500, then passes the money on to each state, county, school and district authority.

Expect your bill during the first week of October. Each stage below tracks the state calendar in KRS 134.015, and the 2026 discount window closed November 1, 2026.

  • October 1 to November 1: 2 percent off.
  • November 2 to December 31: the amount on the bill.
  • January: 5 percent more.
  • February 1 to April 15: a 21 percent charge that bundles the 10 percent penalty with the sheriff's fee.

Online payment carries a fee: $1.50 for a card payment of $60.00 or less, 2.49 percent above that, and $1.50 per ACH or e-check payment. American Express is refused. The site refreshes after 7:00 pm on business days, so a Friday payment may not show until Monday night. On a large bill, ACH avoids the percentage.

sections.h2: Why do two Warren County neighbors pay different rates?
sections.html:
Warren County has two public school districts. Warren County Public Schools serves the county and the outlying parts of Bowling Green, and Bowling Green Independent Schools serves most of the city proper. The city school levy is 84.80 cents against 52.20 cents for the county district, and that single choice moves the bill more than any other line.

Warren County 2025 real estate levies, cents per $100 of assessed value
LevyCents per $100
State10.60
County general fund14.00
Library3.70
Public health2.90
Extension and conservation0.85
City20.30
School, county district52.20
School, city district84.80

The county levies add to 21.45 cents. Put together, the levies yield three totals: 84.25 for land outside any city, 104.55 for city land in the county school district, and 137.15 for city land in the city school district. Ask the sheriff which total applies to your address. Buyers comparing houses across the county will notice the gap.

Owners who are 65 and over, or totally disabled, claim the deduction at the PVA. It is $49,100 for each of 2025 and 2026. A birth certificate, license or passport backs up the age claim.

A disability claim is renewed yearly. Two groups never renew: owners with a service-connected disability, and owners rated permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems. If you sell, tell the PVA so the deduction comes off your old address.

When you visit the PVA, bring photo identification and the proof of age or disability described above. Ask the office to confirm the deduction is on your parcel for the current year before you list, because a buyer will not inherit it. The new owner has to apply for their own if they qualify.

sections.h2: How to contest a Warren County value
sections.html:
Your first stop is a conference with the PVA, (270) 843-3268, because state rules require it before anything else. The roll is open for viewing for thirteen days, beginning the first Monday in May. After meeting with the PVA, file at the County Clerk before the day after inspection ends.

  • Photos, insurance records, building costs and sales listings are the evidence the local board expects.
  • Anyone paid to speak for you must be a professional such as an attorney, accountant, appraiser or broker, and must carry written authority.
  • Hearings start 25 to 35 days after viewing ends and run no more than five days.

Any decision to raise or lower a value arrives with written reasons.

At the close of that day, the sheriff sends every open bill to the clerk as a certificate of delinquency carrying a lien. The clerk keeps accepting payment right up to the annual sale and publishes a PDF list of current delinquent parcels. The sale is held each August at the clerk's office, Suite 100 at 429 E 10th Ave, with buyer registration closing a few days earlier. Call the clerk for this year's date.

Once the bill moves to the clerk, charges stack up fast. Interest runs at 1 percent monthly. The clerk's commission is 10 percent of tax, penalty and interest, and the county attorney adds 20 percent unless the bill is paid within five business days. A $10 lien recording and release fee also applies.

The lien clings to the land for up to eleven years, so it does not disappear when the house sells. Pay it off at closing and get a release from the clerk. Ask the sheriff for a current payoff on this year's bill and the clerk for anything older, and bring both figures to the title company before you sign.

A cash sale can clear an old delinquency from the proceeds without you fronting the money first, which helps if penalties are already piling up. Expect the buyer's title search to turn up every open bill, so it is better to know the total before you list.

A simple order of work helps. First, look up the bill on the sheriff's inquiry page and confirm which school district your parcel sits in. Second, phone the clerk and ask whether any earlier year was sent over as a certificate of delinquency. Third, hand the payoff numbers to whoever handles your closing. Last, ask the clerk for the release once everything is paid, so the lien does not follow the title to the next owner.

Warren County had 149,375 people in mid 2025, and 1,453 building permits were issued during the year. Median rent is $1,002 a month, and 55.6 percent of homes are owner occupied. The median home value is $258,000.

Permits matter at sale time. The county's Division for Building Services, at 1141 State Street, covers everywhere except Bowling Green and Oakland. It charges $0.15 per square foot with a $45 minimum, and sets a fine of at least $500 for work begun without a permit. Sheds from 120 square feet and all pools need one. Phone (270) 843-5360 to ask about a past project before you list.

faqs.q: Which office takes payment for Warren County property tax?
faqs.a: The Warren County Sheriff's Office takes it, at (270) 842-1633. Use the tax inquiry page on its website to look up and pay a bill.

faqs.q: Did the 2026 Warren County discount end?
faqs.a: Yes. The window was October 1 to November 1, 2026. After that the face amount stands until December 31, 2026, and January 2027 adds 5 percent.

faqs.q: Why is the Warren County school tax higher in some places?
faqs.a: The city school district levy is 84.80 cents per $100, against 52.20 cents for the county district. Parcels inside the city's own district pay the higher one.

faqs.q: Does Warren County charge extra to pay by card?
faqs.a: Yes. Card payments run $1.50 up to $60.00 and 2.49 percent over that. ACH and e-check payments cost $1.50, and American Express is not accepted.

faqs.q: What happens to Warren County taxes when I sell?
faqs.a: Any open bill carries a lien on the land for up to eleven years. Pay it at closing and get a release from the clerk.
